def: Software that manages job postings, applications, pipeline stages, interview feedback, and hiring reports; the system of record for recruiting.
Recruiting workflows run by AI agents that take multi-step actions (searching, ranking, drafting outreach, scheduling) with human approval at defined checkpoints.
Using AI models to interpret a role, search public and licensed data for matching people, and rank them, replacing hand-built Boolean searches.
Keyword search using operators such as AND, OR, NOT, and quotation marks to find profiles or resumes in databases and search engines.
A system for nurturing relationships with potential candidates before they apply: talent pools, campaigns, events, and outreach tracking.
A lookup process that queries several contact-data providers in sequence until a verified email or phone number is found.
Advertising spend divided by completed applications; the core metric for programmatic job advertising.
Deliberately building candidate pipelines that reflect the available talent market, often using filters and outreach strategies that reach underrepresented groups.
A short, one-click application flow hosted by a job board that sends candidate data to the employer, trading data completeness for conversion.
The US Fair Credit Reporting Act, which governs employment background checks, including consent, disclosure, and the adverse-action process.
The sequence of stages from application or outreach to hire, analysed by conversion rate at each step.
Human resources information system: the employee system of record for payroll, benefits, and personal data, into which hires flow after the ATS.
LinkedIn's paid messaging product for contacting members outside your network, allocated as monthly credits on Recruiter seats.
Tools that record, transcribe, and analyse interviews to produce notes, scorecards, and interviewer coaching.
Posting a job to many boards and aggregators from one place, usually through the ATS or a distribution service.
A recorded interview in which candidates answer preset questions asynchronously for later review.
Someone not actively looking for a job who may respond to a compelling, personalised approach; the main target of sourcing tools.
Automated buying of sponsored job placements across boards, optimised toward a target cost per application.
A composite measure of how well hires perform and stay, typically combining performance ratings, retention, and manager satisfaction.
Searching an existing ATS database for past applicants who match a new role.
A structured interview feedback form that rates candidates on predefined attributes, enabling consistent comparison.
A strong candidate who reached the final stage but was not hired, and who is worth re-engaging for future roles.
The channel (job board, referral, sourcing tool, agency) that first introduced a hired candidate.
An interview in which every candidate is asked the same job-related questions and rated on the same scale.
Analytics about the external labour market and internal workforce (supply, compensation, skills, competitor movement) used to plan and source.
Days from a candidate's first contact or application to accepted offer; distinct from time to fill, which starts when the requisition opens.
An assessment that asks candidates to perform a realistic piece of the job rather than answer abstract questions.

An AI sourcing agent is software that completes candidate sourcing on its own: given a role brief it searches for candidates, screens and ranks them, finds and verifies contact details, writes and sends personalised email and SMS outreach with follow-ups, and hands engaged candidates to a recruiter. Read more →

Autonomous sourcing is a recruiting model in which an AI agent, not a recruiter, runs the search for candidates: it interprets the role, finds and ranks people, verifies their contact details and reaches out by email and SMS, so recruiters only review shortlists and replies. Read more →

term: AI recruiter vs AI sourcing agent
def: "AI recruiter" is a broad label for any software that does a recruiter's task: screening applications, scheduling, interviewing, note-taking or sourcing. An AI sourcing agent is the specific kind that finds candidates and makes first contact. A product can be both: Noon markets itself as an autonomous AI recruiter and works as a sourcing agent at its core. Read more →
